name: Digital Euro | Operations & Audit Intelligence
tagline: MongoDB Atlas as the operational Single View and unified audit layer for a simulated Digital Euro event architecture.
description: A Next.js operations console that persists five simulated Kafka-style event topics into five MongoDB collections and builds Customer 360 views, transaction state timelines, structured audit search, full-text search, semantic search and dead-letter recovery from those documents. It runs against MongoDB Atlas when MONGODB_URI is set, or uses an in-memory engine that runs the same aggregation pipelines through mingo.
businessProblem: Digital Euro operations produce separate event streams for onboarding, offboarding, DEAN assignment and transactions, outbound notifications, and processing errors. When those streams sit in different stores, reconstructing a customer journey or investigating a failed transaction requires a separate reporting database. This demo shows how a document model, cross-collection aggregation ($unionWith, $lookup, $setWindowFields) and MongoDB Search and Vector Search provide one operational view for audit investigation and error recovery. All data is fictional. The demo does not claim regulatory compliance, exactly-once delivery or production SLAs.

mongodbCapabilities.name: MongoDB Atlas persistence
mongodbCapabilities.description: When MONGODB_URI is set, the app connects to Atlas with the official driver and persists events to five collections in a dedicated demo database. Reset and seed refuse any database whose name does not contain 'demo'. Without MONGODB_URI, an in-memory engine is used instead.

mongodbCapabilities.name: Idempotent append-only ingestion
mongodbCapabilities.description: Events are validated with Zod and checked against state-transition rules, then written with insertMany (ordered: false) behind a unique eventId index, so duplicates are detected rather than overwritten. DLQ management metadata and measured ingestion latency are updated with updateOne and bulk writes. Original business events are never modified.

mongodbCapabilities.name: Cross-collection aggregation pipelines
mongodbCapabilities.description: Dashboard KPIs, Customer 360, transaction timelines and the unified audit stream are built with $unionWith across the five collections, $group/$last for latest-state reconstruction, $facet for paged search, $lookup to find settled transactions without delivered notifications, and $setWindowFields/$shift for previous and next states.

mongodbCapabilities.name: MongoDB Search (full-text)
mongodbCapabilities.description: Creates a de_text Search index on each collection over descriptions, error messages, failure reasons and transition reasons. Runs $search with highlighting on each selected collection and merges the results by normalized score. When the index is missing, the app shows a clearly labeled keyword fallback.

mongodbCapabilities.name: Atlas Vector Search
mongodbCapabilities.description: Embeddings come from the AI SDK through Vercel AI Gateway (default openai/text-embedding-3-small, 256 dimensions) and are stored in an embedding field inside the existing five collections. Queries run $vectorSearch on the de_vector index per collection, and multi-event conditions are then confirmed with deterministic correlation queries. Without embedding credentials, vector search is turned off and the reason is shown.

mongodbCapabilities.name: Simulated Kafka topics
mongodbCapabilities.description: Five logical topics (onboarding-events, offboarding-events, dean-assignment, notification-outbound, error-dead-letter) are simulated, with partitions and offsets labeled as simulated. No Kafka or GCP Pub/Sub broker is integrated. Events are generated on request through /api/simulator/tick.

mongodbCapabilities.name: Change Streams (production option)
mongodbCapabilities.description: Described on the architecture page as a production option for push-based downstream processing. The demo itself refreshes with SWR polling and does not open a change stream.

atlas.notes: Set MONGODB_URI (and optionally MONGODB_DATABASE, which defaults to digital_euro_demo). Then use Event Simulator > Reset and Seed Demo, which seeds in bounded batches, and Ensure indexes, which creates secondary indexes plus the de_text and de_vector search indexes. Search and Vector Search indexes build asynchronously.

configuration.name: MONGODB_URI
configuration.description: MongoDB Atlas connection string. If unset, the app runs in LOCAL DEMO mode with an in-memory engine. Server-side only.

configuration.name: MONGODB_DATABASE
configuration.description: Target database. Defaults to digital_euro_demo. Destructive reset only runs when the name contains 'demo'.

configuration.name: DEMO_MODE
configuration.description: Labels the environment as DEMO. Defaults to true.

configuration.name: DEMO_ADMIN_TOKEN
configuration.description: When set, simulator, DLQ and admin mutations require the x-demo-admin-token header. Recommended for public deployments.

configuration.name: AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
configuration.description: Vercel AI Gateway key for generating embeddings on a local machine. On Vercel, OIDC authentication is automatic.

configuration.name: EMBEDDING_MODEL
configuration.description: AI Gateway embedding model id. Defaults to openai/text-embedding-3-small.

configuration.name: EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS
configuration.description: Embedding dimensions. Defaults to 256. Must match numDimensions of the de_vector index.

configuration.name: ATLAS_SEARCH_INDEX
configuration.description: MongoDB Search index name. Defaults to de_text.

configuration.name: ATLAS_VECTOR_INDEX
configuration.description: Atlas Vector Search index name. Defaults to de_vector.

architecture.overview: Simulated event producers feed a Zod validation and state-transition pipeline. The pipeline writes idempotently to five MongoDB collections. Next.js route handlers run aggregation, $search and $vectorSearch pipelines over those collections to drive the dashboard, Customer 360, transaction explorer, audit search, semantic investigation and DLQ console.
